title: Model anonymous floor, chair and role transitions
summary: Evaluate whether recognition and interaction evidence improves anonymous speaker continuity and floor tracking. Separate floor holder, speaking track, meeting role and verified person; model chair changes and exceptions explicitly.
out_of_scope: Using named recognition as acoustic identity verification
Updating production speaker tracks, enrollments or human confirmations
implementation: Create role/floor candidate records from procedural events and supplied roster context, keeping names as separate permitted evidence views and source-backed role intervals.
Define hypotheses for recognition granted, floor taken, interruption, invitation to answer, backchannel and return to chair; retain contradictions between expected role and observed voice.
Track chair substitutes, temporary chair, reconvened body, prepared statement and shared-mic context as distinct regimes rather than a single session-wide label.
Run deterministic sequence and optional narrow semantic variants on fixed inputs; compare anonymous consistency and floor outcomes before assessing named-candidate benefit.
Export only evidence compatibility and uncertainty plus the implicated source spans to the experimental assessment.

acceptance.criterion: Chair/floor/track/person identities remain different fields and no compatibility result creates an enrollment.
acceptance.verification: Validate outputs and instrument all writes in a synthetic run.

acceptance.criterion: A recognized person who remains silent and a chair who yields are not forced into the next speech turn.
acceptance.verification: Use independently labeled exception cases and compare event/state/track hypotheses.

acceptance.criterion: Role transitions are time-scoped and preserve uncertainty through shared microphones and overlaps.
acceptance.verification: Replay a substituted-chair/multi-body sequence and inspect alternative states.

acceptance.criterion: Reported benefit is measured on the same frozen queries and includes role-conflict misses.
acceptance.verification: Compare variants with fixed acoustic candidates and independent floor labels; report unchanged/worse cases as well as gains.

tests: Speaker 1 is an announcer, not chair
Chair yields and speaks later as ordinary member
Recognized member is absent/silent and another responds
risks: Repeated meeting structure can create strong but wrong person shortcuts.
Existing diarizer tracks may already mix voices.

reuse.application: Use track-is-not-person and unverified upstream claim boundaries.
Reuse phase/floor evidence rather than creating a separate procedural history.

sources: jevinmatter: recognition and anonymous consistency proposal.
